To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HBx expression in hepatocytes results in the accumulation 8-oxoguanine in the genome and the culture supernatant, which is mediated by down-regulating the expression of Mth1 and Mth2, the two key enzymes that are responsible for the sanitization of oxidized nucleotids in hepatocytes.
HBx expression in hepatocytes significantly increases 8-oxoguanine (8-OG) level and reduces the expression of Mth1 and Mth2 at both mRNA level and protein level.
HBx can induce accumulation of 8-OxodG in hepatocellular carcinoma cells through attenuating MTH1/2 expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of HBV X protein on the expression of MHT1/2 and the level of 8-OxodG.
the mechanism of HBV-induced hepatocarcinogenesis, which may provide a new insight into the pathogenesis of HBV-related liver cancer.
the mechanism of HBx-induced oxidative stress in hepatoma cells and the effect of the HBx on Mth1/2 expression and 8-oxoguanine level in hepatoma cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HBx may be a key factor in the development of HBV-related HCC.

HBx expression induces oxidative stress, increases 8-oxogdG production and inhibits the expression of MHT1 and MTH1, which leads to the accumulation of 7,8-DH2-dG in hepatocytes, which may play an important role in liver carcinogenesis.

HBV infection and HBx expression increase the production and accumulation of 7,8-DH2-dG and 8-oxdG in hepatocytes, thus contributing to the mutagenic potential of HBV and its oncogenic role in hepatocarcinogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HBx can induce the accumulation of 7,8-dimethyl-2-oxo-2,3-dihydro-1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]indol-1-yl-8-oxo-dG (DMOX) and 8-OH-dG, which are two major oxidative DNA damage products, through repressing MTH1 and/or MTH2 expression, and that HBx-induced oxidative DNA damage may play an important role
HBx can increase the production of 8-ohdG in hepatocytes through downregulating the expression of Mth1/2, thus contributing to the development of hepatocarcinogenesis.
HBV and its encoded protein HBx could be a double hit for the liver carcinogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HBV X protein can promote the accumulation of oxidized DNA damage in hepatocytes by suppressing MTH1 and/or MTH2 expression.
HBV X protein can increase 8-OxodG level via repressing the expression of Mth1/Mth2 in hepatocytes.
HBx expression increases oxidative DNA damage and mutational risk in hepatocytes through downregulating the expression of Mth1/Mth2.
